Team — forwarding the dataset from FinTech Prospects (they sent ~120 de-id prompts). Notes from call & initial summary of our quick comparative run:

What we ran (quick smoke, small batch): Redwood-instruct-v2 (quantized), Bedrock-standard, Vertex-codex-like.
Initial results (smoke run, ~120 prompts):
- Hallucination rate (regulatory Q&A): Redwood-instruct-v2 = 2.1% | Bedrock = 3.8% | Vertex = 4.5%
- Instruction-following (pass @ threshold): Redwood = 92% | Bedrock = 87% | Vertex = 84%
- Latency (median / p95 for short prompts): Redwood = 160ms / 310ms | Bedrock = 190ms / 420ms | Vertex = 180ms / 460ms
- Token cost (est. per 1k input+output tokens): Redwood = $0.70 | Bedrock = $0.95 | Vertex = $1.10 (note: these are blended infra + license estimates for apples-to-apples)

Caveats: small sample, not instrumented for long-context or streaming differences, and we used a quantized runtime that may slightly affect rare-token behavior. We logged examples of hallucinations and attached them (hallucination_examples.pdf).

Requested next tests from Sales/AE side (what I want from Engineering):
1) Regression checks: rerun with full eval harness, random seed sweep, and check for spurious token generation on the 12 flagged prompts (see hallucination_examples.pdf).
2) Long-context behavior: re-evaluate a subset with 3k-5k token context to measure instruction-following drift and memory of previous messages.
3) Streaming/partial-output behavior: ensure early stopping heuristics and prefix caching don't increase hallucination on streaming outputs.
4) Cost sensitivity: repeat with batching and different quantization profiles and produce a per-config cost vs hallucination chart.

Deliverables & timeline proposal:
- Full regression harness run + report by Tue (7/28)
- Long-context and streaming checks by Fri (7/31)
- Short summary (one pager) for Sara with recommended config and expected unit economics by Mon (8/3)

Attachments included: eval_summary_table.xlsx, hallucination_examples.pdf

Marissa
